items.title: New data, same problem: No Surprises Act arbitration abuse persists - Niskanen Center
items.reason: The item addresses implementation problems and potential abuse within the No Surprises Act's Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) arbitration process, which is a core component of the Act's enforcement mechanism relevant to revenue-cycle operations.
items.summary: The Niskanen Center reports on new data showing continued problems with abuse within the No Surprises Act's Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) arbitration process. The analysis indicates that arbitration is not functioning as intended to protect patients and providers from surprise billing, suggesting systemic issues with how the federal rule is being implemented in practice. This matters for revenue-cycle teams because IDR arbitration outcomes directly affect claim payment determinations, reimbursement rates, and compliance obligations under the No Surprises Act's balance-billing protections.
